info.bio: Nacida en Jamaica en 1946, hija de un capataz de una plantación de azucar. En 1963 se fue a Inglaterra donde hizo su cuarta grabación, una versión de la canción "My Boy Lollipop", la que llegó a ser un superhit, consiguiendo el número dos en listas del Reino Unido y en Estados Unidos. Su estilo podría englobarse en ska, blue beat y reggae.

scenes.name: El soul conquista Gran Bretaña
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: El 26 de octubre «Reach Out I’ll Be There» de los Four Tops, con la flauta de aire oriental, el fraseo dylaniano de Lamont Dozier y la interpretación de su vida de Levi Stubbs, desbancó a «Distant Drums» y fue número 1: el momento en que la música negra americana ocupó el centro de la cultura juvenil británica, al revés que en el boom del beat. Lo habían preparado durante años los entusiastas: Dave Godin, que fundó en 1963 la Tamla Motown Appreciation Society, viajó a Detroit, llevó «Where Did Our Love Go» a los piratas y bautizó el sello Tamla Motown (marzo de 1965, con una gira de la revista que fracasó fuera de Londres); Guy Stevens, que pinchaba discos negros en el Scene y dirigió Sue Records para Chris Blackwell; Roger Eagle en el Twisted Wheel de Mánchester; Tony Hall promocionando Atlantic («In the Midnight Hour», el «My Girl» de Otis Redding); el DJ Jeff Dexter mezclando soul y ska en Tiles, el club subterráneo de Oxford Street del mod de masas que visitó Tom Wolfe. En otoño de 1966 Atlantic y Motown copaban las listas; Otis Redding metió a 8.000 personas en Tiles; los Four Tops arrasaron en el Savile de Brian Epstein el 13 de noviembre. El racismo, aun así, seguía ahí.

podcast.title: Romantic Link to Peter Asher (1964)
podcast.body: Millie Small was romantically associated with Peter Asher, who was one half of the popular British pop duo Peter and Gordon, during the height of her international fame. "She was romantically linked to Peter Asher of Peter and Gordon."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: UK Television Appearances (1964)
podcast.body: Following the success of "My Boy Lollipop," Millie gained significant media attention, including her own UK TV special. She also made an appearance on "Around the Beatles," a special produced by Jack Good and starring The Beatles. "She got her own UK TV special, as well as appearing on Around the Beatles, a special starring the Beatles and produced by Jack Good."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Later Life and Death (1970s-2019)
podcast.body: Millie Small ceased performing after the early 1970s and maintained a private life, giving only one brief interview in 2016. Despite talk of a comeback in the early 1980s, she never returned to performing. She passed away last year at the age of 72. "She died last year, aged 72."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Decline in Success and Poverty (1960s-2000s)
podcast.body: After the initial wave of Ska's popularity subsided, Millie struggled to replicate her early success despite numerous attempts and collaborations. She subsequently spent much of the following decades in poverty, never receiving significant financial benefits from her massive chart achievements. "Millie spent much of the next few decades in poverty."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Early Life and Discovery (1960s)
podcast.body: Millie Small started performing at the age of 12, winning Kingston's biggest talent contest, the Vere Johns' Opportunity Hour. At 14, in 1962, her voice, noted for its spooky resemblance to Shirley Goodman of Shirley and Lee, attracted the attention of producer Coxsone Dodd, leading to her first recordings. "Millie Small had started performing at the age of 12, when she won the Vier jumps opportunity hour, the single biggest talent contest in Kingston."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: First International Ska Star
podcast.body: Millie Small became Ska's first international star following the success of "My Boy Lollipop" in 1964. Her career marked the first significant impact of a Jamaican artist on the music charts in both Britain and America. "a 14-year-old girl who would become Scar's first international star."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Jamaican Honors (Later Life)
podcast.body: Despite her financial struggles, Millie Small was recognized and honored multiple times by the people of Jamaica for her pioneering musical achievements, including being made a Commander in the Order of Distinction. "She was given multiple honors by the people of Jamaica, including being made a commander in the order of distinction, but never really got any financial benefit from her enormous child success."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

xref.title: Producer of Millie Small's Hit
xref.body: Chris Blackwell, an Englishman, produced Millie Small's worldwide hit "My Boy Lollipop." This song was a significant milestone in bringing Jamaican Ska (SCOP/Blue Beat) music to a broader audience in Britain and internationally, facilitated by his newly established Island Records label. "The big breakthrough was a worldwide hit by Millie Small, called My Boy Lollipop, produced by Englishman Chris Blackwell, and distributed through his brand new Idle and Records label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
